key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power and welding current strengthen molten-pool convection and penetration, while higher welding speed reduces heat input and shrinks the weld; arc stability depends strongly on these parameters.
engineering_relevance: These results help tune hybrid welding settings to achieve controlled penetration, weld width, and arc behavior for high-precision Invar steel fabrication.
method: Numerical simulation of molten-pool flow and keyhole behavior
High-speed photography of arc and pool dynamics
Parametric study of laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative simulation and high-speed imaging results across laser power, welding speed, and current ranges, linking parameter changes to penetration, weld width, flow, and arc stability.
watch_item: The findings are parameter-window specific, so process optimization should be validated for the exact joint geometry, shielding conditions, and machine setup used in practice.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
